comment: File-based allow-list for the browser MCP server: one entry per role, naming exactly the browser tools that role may call.

The server reads this file at startup and checks it as the first statement of every tool. A (role, tool) pair that is not listed here is refused with an authorization_denied error naming the role, the tool and the roles that ARE allowed, and the refusal is journalled to the same audit log that records the successful calls.
A role that is absent from 'roles' is an unknown role and is refused, as is a missing or blank role; nothing is defaulted to an allowed role. An empty list means the role is known and holds nothing.

Derived from docs/routing-and-tool-grant-map.json: every 'mcp__browser__<tool>' string under 'grants.<role>' becomes a grant here, and nothing else does. The server refuses to start when this file and that map's projection disagree, once the map carries the browser server; while it does not, the server starts with a warning and this file governs.

The beta tester is the only role that holds the browser tools: it uses the running app instead of reading the repository, so the other roles have no reason to reach a page, and their absence here is the same statement their grants make in the routing map.
Written as valid JSON with no comments: the explanation lives in these string fields.
derivation: grants[role] filtered to the operations this server exposes (mcp__browser__*); the eight tools are granted to beta-tester alone and every other role's list is empty

denial_note_by_role.orchestrator: refused every browser tool: it sequences roles and reads their returns, and drives no page itself
denial_note_by_role.planner: refused every browser tool: a plan is written from the ticket and the repository, and the running app is not its evidence
denial_note_by_role.implementer: refused every browser tool: it changes the code and runs the gates, and the browser evidence belongs to the role that tests the built app
denial_note_by_role.tester: refused every browser tool: it runs the configured gates over the tree, and a browser session is the beta tester's surface, not the gate's
denial_note_by_role.reviewer: refused every browser tool: it reviews the diff and the journal, and it reaches no page to form a verdict
denial_note_by_role.project-manager: refused every browser tool: it owns ticket state, not application behaviour
denial_note_by_role.researcher: refused every browser tool: its channel is the open web through its own search tool, and the app under test is not a research source

denial_note_by_tool.browser_open: refused to every role but beta-tester, so only the role whose evidence is the app's behaviour can reach a page, and its target stays inside the base origin
denial_note_by_tool.browser_snapshot: refused to every role but beta-tester: the text-first page view exists to record what the app showed the tester
denial_note_by_tool.browser_click: refused to every role but beta-tester: navigating the app is a testing act, never a build or review step
denial_note_by_tool.browser_type: refused to every role but beta-tester: entering text into the app is part of exercising it
denial_note_by_tool.browser_press: refused to every role but beta-tester: key events belong to the same interaction the tester drives
denial_note_by_tool.browser_diagnostics: refused to every role but beta-tester: the console, page-error and request evidence is the tester's finding, drained as it reads it
denial_note_by_tool.browser_screenshot: refused to every role but beta-tester: a PNG is the tester's evidence file under .memory
denial_note_by_tool.browser_close: refused to every role but beta-tester: the session it opened is the one it closes
